title: Status orchestration and staged customer notices + operator playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This document defines the operator-facing playbook for orchestrating the public status page and staged customer notices during LLM-serving incidents. It focuses on: bridge orchestration, consistent staged messaging (legal-safe), status page cadence, escalation triggers tied to SLOs, and post-incident evidence collection that satisfies both engineering and customer/legal needs.

Audience
- On-call bridge operators
- SRE rotation leads
- Customer Success (for major incidents)
- Legal and Compliance (notification hooks)

Why this exists
- Reduce variability in customer-facing messages.
- Ensure status page updates are accurate, timely, and legally safe.
- Provide a concise operator checklist that ties monitoring signals -> bridge actions -> customer notices.

Table of contents
1) Pre-incident preparation
2) Activation decision ladder
3) Bridge orchestration (operator run steps)
4) Status page cadence (templates and timeline)
5) Message templates (severity tiers)
6) Customer notice governance and legal-safe language rules
7) Post-incident evidence checklist + postmortem template snippet
8) Game day / exercise plan
9) Ownership and escalation matrix
10) References and related links

1) Pre-incident preparation
- Daily: verify statuspage API token (secret manager path: secrets/statuspage/api-token) and bridge bot token.
- Weekly: smoke the status page pipeline by sending a test event to the staging page (CLI):
  - redwoodctl statuspage send-test --page staging --summary "smoke" --group "ops"
- Ensure the following artifacts are current in the runbook folder: incident runbook ID, customer impact list (CSV), regulatory contact list.
- SLOs to keep in mind:
  - API availability: 99.95% monthly. Major-alert threshold: 99.5% over 30m rolling.
  - Generative request p99 latency: target <400ms; degradation alert if p99 >= 900ms for 5m.
  - Token error rate: target <0.3%; major if >=1% for 10m.

Checklist table (for on-call console pre-shift):
| Item | Location / Command | Owner | Verified |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Statuspage token | secrets/statuspage/api-token | Oncall | yes/no |
| Bridge bot integration | Slack #incidents-app | Oncall | yes/no |
| Customer impact CSV | /runbooks/affected-tenants.csv | CS | yes/no |

2) Activation decision ladder
1. Alert fires (monitoring > threshold).
2. Quick triage (first 5 minutes): scope (single model / region / multi-tenant?) and severity estimate.
3. If evidence indicates customer-visible degradation (error rate >0.5% OR p99>900ms OR >5% traffic dropped): open bridge and post initial status.
4. If only degraded internal metrics (no customer errors observed) continue internal triage and schedule a watch; escalate to bridge if uncertain after 15 minutes.

Decision checklist (first 10 minutes):
- Who is impacted? (list tenants, affected endpoints)
- What is the observed impact? (latency, errors, missing responses)
- Is a rollback or model fallback required?
- Are there regulatory customers that need immediate direct notification? (see /runbooks/regulatory-contacts.csv)

3) Bridge orchestration (operator run steps)
1. Open the operator bridge:
   - Command: redwoodctl bridge open --service serving-runtime --incident-id $INCIDENT_ID --summary "Initial triage: [short summary]"
   - Slack: /invite @oncall @sre-lead to #bridge-$INCIDENT_ID
2. Post the initial incident stub to status page (see templates below). Use the statuspage API UI or:
   - redwoodctl statuspage create --page production --summary "Investigating increased errors for /v1/generate" --impact "partial_outage" --components "API,Generation" --incident-id $INCIDENT_ID
3. Assign primary roles in the bridge (document in bridge header):
   - Bridge operator (owner of comms and timeline)
   - Triage lead (drives debugging and RCA)
   - Mitigation lead (executes rollbacks/fallbacks)
   - CS liaison (customer notices and direct enterprise comms)
   - Legal contact (if regulated tenant affected)
4. Collect evidence artifacts (commands):
   - kubectl -n serving logs -l app=runtime --since=10m > /tmp/logs-$INCIDENT_ID.txt
   - redwoodctl metrics query "rate(errors[10m])" --service serving-runtime --output csv > /tmp/errors-$INCIDENT_ID.csv
   - Snapshot current routes and model pins: redwoodctl routes list --format json > /tmp/routes-$INCIDENT_ID.json
5. If mitigation requires immediate action, document the action with timestamps in bridge and on status page updates.
6. Maintain a running timeline in the bridge header and update every 15 minutes or after a major milestone.

4) Status page cadence (templates and timeline)
Use the following cadence for incidents that meet customer-impact criteria. If the incident is short (<15m) a single update is acceptable.
- Initial post: within 10 minutes of opening bridge. Mark impact as investigating or partial_outage.
- Follow-up: every 15 minutes while active or when there is a material change.
- Mitigation complete: when a fix or viable fallback is applied.
- All-clear and detailed postmortem: within 72 hours for major incidents (>1 hour or affecting enterprise customers).

Status page timeline table:
| Time from detection | Action | Template name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0-10m | Initial stub (investigating) | initial-investigating |
| 10-30m | First follow-up (scope + ETA if known) | followup-scope-eta |
| every 15m | Progress update | progress-update |
| mitigation complete | Mitigation notice | mitigation-applied |
| 24-72h | Post-incident summary + link to postmortem | postmortem-published |

5) Message templates (severity tiers)
All templates below use replacement tokens: {INCIDENT_ID}, {SERVICE}, {IMPACT}, {ETA}, {ACTIONS}, {CUSTOMER_LANES}. Keep language neutral and factual. Legal-safe rules in next section.

Severity: Informational / Degraded (low)
- Public status page: "[{INCIDENT_ID}] We are investigating intermittent latency affecting {SERVICE}. Some requests may see slower responses. Engineers are actively investigating. We will post updates within 30 minutes."
- Private customer notice (CS): "We observed intermittent latency on {SERVICE} that may affect request latency; no data loss detected. We are investigating and will follow up with timeline and mitigation steps. If you are seeing errors, please share request ids."

Severity: Partial outage (medium)
- Public status page: "[{INCIDENT_ID}] Partial outage: Short interruptions to {SERVICE} are impacting a subset of customers. Our team is in the bridge and working on mitigation. Estimated next update: {ETA}."
- Enterprise direct notice (CS + Legal-safe): "We are currently experiencing an incident (ID {INCIDENT_ID}) impacting {SERVICE}. We are actively mitigating and will provide a timeline and a post-incident report. At this time there is no evidence of customer data exposure. If you require an immediate call, please reply to this message and include preferred contacts."

Severity: Major outage (high)
- Public status page: "[{INCIDENT_ID}] Major outage affecting {SERVICE}. Customers may experience interruptions across regions. We have invoked our mitigation plan and are prioritizing recovery. Next update: {ETA}."
- Enterprise legal-safe notice: "We are experiencing a major service interruption (ID {INCIDENT_ID}) impacting production {SERVICE}. Our priority is recovery and protecting customer data. We will provide an interim update within {ETA} and a full post-incident report within 72 hours. For questions about regulatory obligations, contact compliance@redwood.example.com."

Internal Slack stub (bridge channel): "INCIDENT {INCIDENT_ID} - {SERVICE} - {IMPACT}. Triage: {TRIAGE_SUMMARY}. Roles: bridge_op=@{BRIDGE_OP}, triage=@{TRIAGE}, mitig=@{MITIG}. Evidence artifacts: /tmp/logs-{INCIDENT_ID}."

6) Customer notice governance and legal-safe language rules
- Never speculate about data exposure. If you do not know, state "no evidence of customer data exposure at this time" until Legal advises otherwise.
- Avoid promises of timelines unless confident. Use ETA windows and update frequently.
- For regulated customers (financial, healthcare), always CC Compliance and Legal on enterprise notices.
- For incidents requiring credits or contractual remediation, route to Billing with the incident ID and impacted tenant list; do not commit credits over Slack.

7) Post-incident evidence checklist + postmortem template snippet
Evidence to collect before closure:
- Monitoring exports: 30m pre-incident and incident window metrics in CSV.
- Log bundle: serving runtime logs for affected pods/nodes, compressed tar.gz with clear naming /evidence/inc-$INCIDENT_ID/logs.tar.gz.
- Route and deployment snapshot: model pins, route table, recent deploy IDs (git SHA).
- Mitigation actions and timestamps: who executed, commands run, rollbacks, fallback model IDs.
- Customer-facing timeline: every public status update copy and time posted.

Postmortem template (fill in key sections):
- Title: Short descriptive title + incident ID.
- Severity and impact: affected services, tenant count, duration, business impact estimate.
- Timeline: minute-level timeline with actions and owners.
- Root cause analysis: concise cause and contributing factors.
- Mitigations and permanent fixes: short-term, medium-term, long-term.
- Lessons learned and follow-ups: assign engineering owners and target dates.
- Evidence artifacts: links to metrics, logs, runbook commands.

8) Game day / exercise plan
Objective: Practice status page pipeline, staged notices, and enterprise comms under time pressure.
- Frequency: quarterly.
- Participants: SREs, oncall engineers, CS, Legal (observer), Product (observer).
- Scenario types: KV cache eviction causing p99 latency spikes; model fallback misrouting; tokenization/encoder crash affecting embed pipeline.
- Success criteria: initial status posted within 10 minutes, follow-ups every 15 minutes, enterprise CS notice sent within 30 minutes for impacted customers, postmortem published within 48 hours for exercise.

Checklist for game day run:
1. Start timer at alert firing.
2. Operator opens test bridge and posts to staging status page.
3. CS crafts an enterprise notice using templates; Legal reviews only if scenario includes data exposure.
4. Run through mitigation steps and perform a simulated rollback.
5. End play and capture timeline artifacts.

9) Ownership and escalation matrix
- Bridge operator: primary on-call (starts bridge, comms). Escalation: @sre-lead if >30m unresolved.
- Triage lead: senior on-call engineer. Escalation: runtime owners group.
- Mitigation lead: deployment/runbook owners. Escalation: platform eng director.
- CS liaison: enterprise CS lead. Escalation: Head of CS and Legal for regulated tenants.

10) References and related links
- Incident communications and postmortem framework: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026
- Statuspage API docs (internal): /internal-docs/statuspage-api
- Bridge tooling: /confluence/eng-sre/tools/bridge-operator-guide

Appendix: quick copy/paste templates
- Initial status page (short):
  "[{INCIDENT_ID}] Investigating increased errors for {SERVICE}. Engineers are investigating; next update in 15 minutes."

- Enterprise short notice (email/CS channel):
  Subject: "Incident {INCIDENT_ID} impacting {SERVICE} - immediate update"
  Body: "Hello {CUSTOMER_NAME},

  We are currently investigating an incident affecting {SERVICE}. Our engineers are working on mitigation. At this time, there is no evidence of customer data exposure. Next update: {ETA}.

  For urgent escalation reply to this thread or call {CS_PHONE}.

  - Redwood Inference Ops"

- Internal command snippets to gather artifacts:
  kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=runtime -o wide
  redwoodctl metrics query "histogram_latency_seconds_bucket{quantile=\"0.99\"}" --service serving-runtime --since 15m --output csv
  redwoodctl routes snapshot --output /tmp/routes-$INCIDENT_ID.json
